name: First steps in faith
description: A gentle first week for anyone new to following Jesus: grace, prayer, the Bible, church and what comes next.

days.title: A new beginning
days.note: A respected teacher comes to Jesus at night with questions. Jesus tells him about being born again.
days.devotional:
Jesus tells Nicodemus that a person needs a new birth from God. A religious background, church attendance, or good behaviour cannot save us. We have sinned and need the rescue Jesus provides through His death for our sins and His resurrection.

The response is repentance toward God and personal faith in Jesus Christ as Saviour. Salvation is God’s gift by grace, not something we earn. If you have not personally trusted Christ, explore the plan “The good news: trusting Jesus” and talk with a trusted pastor. Repeating a prayer or completing a plan cannot save you; Jesus saves.
days.prayer: God, help me understand the new birth Jesus describes. Lead me to honest repentance and personal trust in Christ, and help me grow in Your word.
questions: What questions do you bring to Jesus, like Nicodemus did?
What does it mean to you that faith starts with God's love?

days.title: Saved by grace
days.note: Paul explains what God has done for us in Christ — and why none of it is earned.
days.devotional:
Grace means a gift you could never earn. Paul says we were dead, and God made us alive. That is not a reward; it is rescue.

And the story continues: we are His workmanship, created for good works He has prepared. Good works do not save us; they flow from being saved.
days.prayer: Father, help me understand salvation by grace through faith. For those who have trusted Christ, grow grateful obedience that flows from Your gift.
questions: Why is it good news that salvation can't be earned?
What 'good works' might God have prepared for you?

days.title: Free from condemnation
days.note: This chapter begins with one of the most freeing sentences in the Bible.
days.devotional:
Many new believers still feel the weight of past failures. Paul's first words here speak straight to that: in Christ, there is no condemnation left for you.

God's Spirit now lives in you, and He reminds you that you are God's child. You can call Him 'Abba', Father.
days.prayer: Abba, Father, thank You that there is no condemnation for me in Christ. Thank You for making me Your child.
questions: What guilt or shame do you need to leave behind?
How does it feel to call God 'Father'?

days.title: Learning to pray
days.note: Jesus teaches His followers how to pray, and gives them words to start with.
days.devotional:
Prayer is simply talking with God. Jesus says you don't need many words or a show; your Father sees in secret.

The Lord's Prayer is a good place to start: praise, His kingdom, daily needs, forgiveness, and protection. Try praying through it slowly today, in your own words.
days.prayer: Father, teach me to pray. Help me talk with You honestly, every day.
questions: Which line of the Lord's Prayer means most to you right now?
When in your day could you set aside a few quiet minutes to pray?

days.title: God's word for you
days.note: The longest psalm is a love song about God's word.
days.devotional:
The writer loves God's word because it brings wisdom, direction and joy. It gives enough light for the next step.

You don't have to understand everything at once. A little each day, read slowly and prayerfully, will light your path.
days.prayer: Lord, let Your word light my next step and my path. Give me a love for reading it, and help me live it out.
questions: What makes reading the Bible hard for you, and what could help?
What would a simple daily rhythm of reading look like for you?

days.title: Together
days.note: The first Christians did not follow Jesus alone. See what their life together looked like.
days.devotional:
Faith grows best in community. The first believers devoted themselves to teaching, fellowship, sharing meals and prayer.

If you are not yet part of a church family, this is a good week to take a step towards one. You were never meant to walk alone.
days.prayer: Lord, thank You for Your church. Lead me to people I can grow with, and help me love them well.
questions: Which part of the early church's life together appeals to you most?
What step could you take towards a church community?

days.title: Sent out
days.note: The risen Jesus sends His followers out, with a promise to be with them always.
days.devotional:
Jesus' last words in Matthew give every follower a purpose: help others follow Him too. That can start small — sharing what this week has meant to you.

And He ends with a promise to hold onto: He will be with you always.
days.prayer: Jesus, thank You for being with me always. Help me share Your love with someone this week.
questions: Who could you tell about your first week of following Jesus?
What will you keep doing after this plan ends?
